gap: No result ChatGPT got states, in a music service's own words, why streaming downloads can't fill these players: Spotify's user agreement (last updated 2026-09-04) says users "will not redistribute, sell or transfer the Spotify Service or the Content". Every pick under $100 therefore only plays music files the shopper already owns, copied over USB.
standout_why: I compared against soundmavericks.com (cited), our own page, and the Shokz MP3-storage blog. Soundmavericks already explains the main reason swim headphones need onboard music: "Bluetooth runs on 2.4GHz radio waves, and water absorbs that signal almost immediately". It also gives per-model format lists and says "no swimming headphone can store offline copies from a streaming app by itself", but it never says why. ChatGPT's own answers already warned that Spotify and Apple Music downloads won't work, without a source. So the reason Bluetooth fails underwater is already covered. The Spotify clause only adds the service's own wording to a point rivals partly make. I couldn't open the WIRED, TechRadar or Verywell Fit pages (blocked or empty), so I can't rule out that they also have it.
decides: It doesn't change the pick. It confirms that onboard storage is required, which the MOJAWA Run Plus, Jabees 7Seven and Shokz OpenSwim Pro all have. It does add one condition for the shopper: a Spotify or Apple Music subscriber with no owned files can't fill any of these players, whatever the price. Format support doesn't separate the picks either: the Run Plus spec lists MP3, WAV, AAC, FLAC, M4A and APE, close to the Shokz list, so iTunes-purchased AAC/M4A files should play on both.
